title: Yellowstone's Upper Loop, then on to Glacier
summary: Finish Yellowstone's Upper 8 loop clockwise, then drive north-west toward West Glacier via Bozeman and Butte.
drive: Canyon Village to West Glacier via Bozeman and Butte · 9h · 720 km

segments.name: Segment 1 — Gibbon Falls to Norris Geyser Basin
segments.blurb: A waterfall and two short-hike geyser basins on the way to Norris.

map.to: Norris Geyser Basin, Yellowstone National Park

stops.name: Gibbon Falls
stops.note: Roadside waterfall on the Gibbon River.

stops.name: Beryl Spring
stops.note: Small, loud hot spring right by the road.

stops.name: Monument Geyser Basin
stops.note: Steep short hike to a ridge of geyser cones.

stops.name: Artists' Paintpots
stops.note: Boardwalk loop past mudpots and hot springs.

stops.name: Norris Geyser Basin
stops.note: Hottest, most acidic basin in the park.

trail.from: Norris Geyser Basin parking lot / Norris Museum
trail.caveat: Porcelain Basin and Back Basin are two separate loops, not one trail

expect.arrive: Gibbon Falls and Beryl Spring are both direct roadside pull-offs, no real walk. Norris has the biggest lot on this stretch and is the hottest, most acidic basin in the park; it's split into two separate boardwalk loops (Porcelain Basin and Back Basin) that don't connect at both ends, so plan which one(s) you're doing before setting off from the car.
expect.parking: Norris Geyser Basin's lot is large and generally has room outside of midday peak; Gibbon Falls and Beryl Spring are small pull-offs with a handful of spaces each.

paths.do: Gibbon Falls and Beryl Spring from the pull-offs, skip Norris's basins.
Same pull-offs, plus the shorter Porcelain Basin loop at Norris.
Porcelain Basin and Back Basin, the full Norris visit.

alt: Artists Paint Pots mud pots Yellowstone
segments.seasonal: Monument Geyser Basin's trail is a steep 2.4 mi (3.8 km) round trip climbing roughly 800 ft — real hiking, not a stroll (nps.gov/places/000/monument-geyser-basin-trailhead.htm and USGS). Given the no-strenuous-hikes rule, skip it and view the basin's steam plumes from the road instead.

segments.name: Segment 2 — Roaring Mountain to Mammoth Hot Springs
segments.blurb: A steaming hillside, then the park's terraced hot spring complex.

map.from: Norris Geyser Basin, Yellowstone National Park
map.to: Mammoth Hot Springs, Yellowstone National Park

stops.name: Roaring Mountain
stops.note: Acidic hillside vented with steam and fumaroles.

stops.name: Cleopatra Spring and Terrace
stops.note: Travertine terrace within the Mammoth complex.

stops.name: Mammoth Hot Springs
stops.note: Wide travertine terraces, the park's north hub.

expect.arrive: Roaring Mountain is a roadside pull-off with the steaming hillside visible straight from the car. Mammoth's terraces sprawl across a hillside above the village; the Lower Terraces have a boardwalk right off the main lot, the Upper Terraces are reached by a one-way drive loop above them.
expect.parking: Roaring Mountain's pull-off is small; Mammoth has several lots around the village and near the Lower Terraces, generally with room outside of midday.

paths.opt: Roadside and Lower Terraces boardwalk only
paths.do: Roaring Mountain from the pull-off, then the flat lower boardwalk loop at Mammoth.
Same, plus the one-way scenic drive above the terraces with its own pull-offs.

segments.name: Segment 3 — Lamar Valley and Mount Washburn
segments.blurb: Open valley for wildlife, then a high summit lookout before exiting north.

map.from: Mammoth Hot Springs, Yellowstone National Park

stops.name: Slough Creek
stops.note: Prime wildlife-watching meadow, wolves and bison.

stops.name: Yellowstone River Overlook
stops.note: Open view across the Lamar Valley.

stops.name: Mount Washburn
stops.note: Fire lookout summit; wide views of the whole park.

expect.arrive: Lamar Valley's turnouts are wide gravel shoulders right on the road, wildlife visible with the naked eye from the car in many cases. Mount Washburn's trailhead at Dunraven Pass is a real mountain summit hike — this is not a stroll, and the road itself sits at high elevation where a September storm can close it with little warning.
expect.parking: Lamar Valley turnouts are informal gravel pull-offs, plentiful but the best wildlife-viewing spots fill at dawn and dusk; Dunraven Pass trailhead lot is small and can fill on clear days.

paths.opt: Lamar Valley only, drive past Washburn
paths.do: Stop at the wildlife turnouts, continue over Dunraven Pass without stopping.
Same, plus a few minutes at the Dunraven Pass trailhead pull-off for the view without hiking.
The full out-and-back to the fire lookout summit — not recommended for this trip; strenuous, high elevation, real time cost.

segments.seasonal: The road over Dunraven Pass (Canyon to Tower) is scheduled to stay open through late September into October 2026, but it's one of the first roads to close if an early storm hits — check current conditions the morning of. The NPS also flags grizzly bears actively feeding on whitebark pine nuts on Mount Washburn in fall and recommends hiking only in groups of 3+ with bear spray — one more reason the drive-by option fits this trip better than the hike (nps.gov/thingstodo/yell-trail-dunraven-pass-mount-washburn.htm).

segments.name: Segment 4 — Drive to West Glacier via Bozeman and Butte
segments.blurb: Long transit day: out of the park, past Bozeman, through Butte.

stops.name: Yellowstone Hot Springs (Paradise Valley)
stops.note: Riverside soak stop north of the park, [to add].

stops.name: Butte — Berkeley Pit
stops.note: Former open-pit copper mine, now a flooded overlook.

expect.arrive: This is the long transit leg — nine hours of driving from Canyon Village to West Glacier. Bozeman is a normal college-town downtown with metered street parking; Butte's Berkeley Pit has its own small paid viewing-stand lot right at the edge of the flooded pit.
expect.parking: Bozeman downtown has metered spaces and a few public garages; the Berkeley Pit lot in Butte is small but rarely full given the short visit duration.

paths.do: Gas and bathroom stops only, no detours.
Add a 30-45 minute walk through downtown Bozeman for dinner or coffee.
Same Bozeman stop, plus 20-30 minutes at the Berkeley Pit overlook in Butte.
